transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Um, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place. 

Well... my husband kind of pushed me to come in. He and the people at the warehouse where I work, they just... they keep acting like I'm crazy. I don't want to sound difficult or anything, because I'm a really hard worker, I promise. But I just... I know they've been watching my moves on the floor. And they keep changing my pallet counts. 

I know they're just doing it to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. I just want to do a good job and move up, you know? Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I'm explaining it like this.
Do you really believe that people at your workplace are watching you and changing your pallet counts on purpose?

Um... I know it probably sounds a little strange when you say it out loud like that. I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult person or a complainer, because I try so hard to get along with everyone. 

But... yeah. Even though my husband and the warehouse guys keep acting like I'm crazy for bringing it up, I just... I know they've been watching my moves out there on the floor. And the pallet counts really do get changed. I'm just trying to be honest with you, I promise. I just know they're doing it to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

Does that... I mean, is it okay that I feel that way? I'm not trying to cause trouble, I just want to do a good job and be treated fair.
Do you think there's any possibility that the pallet counts are being changed due to an error or a legitimate reason, rather than a plot against you?

Um... I mean, I guess it's possible? I really try to be open-minded, doctor, I swear I do. I don't want to be one of those people who just blames everyone else for their mistakes. 

But... it's just so hard to believe it's a mistake when it happens so much. And the way they look at me... it just feels so real that they're watching me. My husband gets so frustrated with me, and I hate upsetting him, but I just... I really know in my heart they're doing it to stop me from getting that supervisor spot. 

I'm sorry, I know that's not what you probably want to hear. Am I being too stubborn about this? I just... I want to be honest with you so you can help me.
Have you ever had any other thoughts like this, where you felt like someone or something was against you or plotting to hold you back, outside of work?

Um... outside of work? I don't... I don't think so. I really try to get along with everyone, everywhere I go. I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I'm really not. 

It's just... it's just this one thing, with the warehouse. My husband gets so mad when I talk about it, and I know he thinks I'm making it up, but I really, truly know they're watching my moves on the floor and messing with my pallet counts. It's just because of that supervisor spot, I swear. I wouldn't even bring it up if it wasn't happening right in front of me. 

Is it okay that it's just happening at work? I hope I'm answering your questions right. I really want to be helpful.
Do you still believe people at your workplace are watching you and changing your pallet counts when you're not thinking about the supervisor spot?

Um... well... yes. I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm just obsessing over it, because I try so hard not to. But... even when things are a little calmer, you know? Like, there was a quiet few weeks a little while back where I was actually sleeping a bit better, closer to normal, and I wasn't rushing around so much or feeling so wound up... 

But even then, I still... well, I still heard that voice telling me to check my pallets. And I still knew they were messing with the counts to work against me. I'm sorry, I know that sounds bad, and I really wish I could tell you it goes away when I'm feeling calmer. I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. Is it okay that I still felt that way even when I was sleeping better? I hope I'm not making things too complicated.
Do you think it's possible that you might be mistaken about people watching you and changing your pallet counts?

Um... I know you're trying to help me look at all the angles, and I really appreciate that, doctor. I do. I don't want to be difficult or seem like I won't listen to reason. 

But... it's just so hard to say I'm mistaken when it's the whole reason I'm even here. I only came in because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy for saying it. But I just... I know in my gut they've been watching my moves and changing the counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably frustrating for you to hear. I really am trying to be cooperative. Am I being too difficult about this? I just want to be honest about why I'm sitting here talking to you.
Can you think of any evidence that would change your mind about people watching you and changing your pallet counts?

Um... evidence? I mean, I guess... well, I don't know what evidence there could be, because it's just... it's what's happening. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm just being stubborn, and I really, really don't want to be. I want to be open-minded, I promise. But like I was saying before, the whole reason I even agreed to come in and talk to you today is because my husband and the people at the warehouse are acting like I'm crazy for bringing it up. But I just... I know it's real. I know they've been watching my moves on the floor and changing my pallet counts so I don't get that supervisor spot. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm giving you the wrong answer. Am I being too difficult? I just don't know how to change my mind when I know what they're doing. Is it okay that I don't have a better answer for you?
Do you think there's anything that could ever convince you that the people at your workplace are not watching you or changing your pallet counts?

Um... well... I want to say yes, because I know that's probably what you want to hear, and I really want to be helpful. I don't want you to think I'm just completely shut off to anything else. 

But... I just... I keep coming back to the same thing. Like I said, the only reason I'm here is because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy for saying it. But I just know it. I know they've been watching my moves and changing the counts to keep me from getting that supervisor spot. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself and not giving you what you need. I really wish I could say something different to make this easier for you. Am I being too frustrating? I just don't know how to not believe something that feels so real to me. Is that okay?
Have you ever heard voices when no one else is around?

Um... I mean... I really don't want you to think I'm, you know, completely losing my mind or anything. It's not like I'm hearing a whole bunch of scary things or anything like that. 

But... I guess, sometimes, yeah. Like when I'm down in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes... I will hear a man's voice. It's clear as day, even when nobody is anywhere near me. He just tells me, Nicole, check it again. I always look around to see who it is, but it's just me. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds really bad, doesn't it? I hope it's okay that I'm telling you that. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and answering your questions right. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or to express them in a way that makes sense to others?

Um... well... I hope you don't think I'm just rambling or anything. I really try my best to be clear, I promise. But... yeah, I guess sometimes people do say they have a hard time following me. 

It's just that when I try to explain what's going on, you know, with the warehouse... my mind just kind of jumps around a little bit. Like, I'll be talking about the forklift sheets, and then I'll think about the signs outside my church, and then I'll remember the tone of voice my husband was using... and it all makes sense in my head, but when it comes out, people tell me they can't understand what I'm trying to say. 

I'm really trying to do better with it, though. I don't want to be confusing. Am I making sense to you right now? I hope I'm not talking too much or jumping around too much for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you often find yourself losing your train of thought when talking to others?

Um... well... I guess that's kind of what I was just trying to say, actually. I hope I didn't already mess up your questions by jumping ahead. I really want to do this right for you. 

But yeah, I do lose my train of thought sometimes. Like I mentioned, when I'm trying to explain everything that's going on, my words just kind of run together. I'll start on the forklift sheets, and then suddenly I'm talking about the church signs, and then my husband's tone of voice... and I know it probably sounds like a mess to everyone else. People do tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. 

I really try hard to stay on track, I promise I do. I don't want to be difficult to talk to. Is it okay that I'm repeating myself a little bit? I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking me.
Do you often find it hard to stick to one topic when talking to others?

Oh... um, yes. I think that's exactly what I was just trying to say. I'm so sorry, I hope I'm not frustrating you by repeating myself, I really want to be helpful and do this right for you. 

But yes, sticking to one thing is exactly where I get tripped up. Like I was mentioning before... when I try to explain what's going on, my words just kind of run all together. I'll go from the forklift sheets at work, straight to the church signs, and then to my husband's tone... and I don't even always realize I'm not on the same topic anymore until people tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. 

I really am trying to work on it, though, so I don't bother people with it. Does that make sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the answers you need.
Do you often have trouble organizing your thoughts in your head before you try to express them to others?

Um... yeah, I do. I'm sorry, I feel like I keep giving you the exact same answer, and I really don't want to waste your time or be annoying. I hope I'm doing okay. 

But yes, organizing it in my head first... that's the hard part. It all feels connected up there, but then when I open my mouth to explain what's going on, it just spills out wrong. My words will run straight from the forklift sheets at the warehouse, over to the church signs, and then to my husband's tone of voice. And I don't mean to do it, I really try to keep it neat, but people tell me they just can't follow what I'm saying. 

I'm trying my best to think before I speak, I really am. Am I making sense to you right now? I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient for you.
Do you feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words most of the time?

Oh, gosh... I must be doing a really bad job of answering if you have to keep asking me this. I am so, so sorry. I really don't mean to be difficult or make your job harder. 

But yes, disjointed is probably the perfect word for it. It's just like I've been trying to say... when I try to explain what is going on, my words just run all over the place. I'll go from the forklift sheets, right to the church signs, and then to my husband's tone. It's hard to put into words because it all feels connected to me, but then people tell me they can't follow what I'm saying at all. 

I hope I'm not frustrating you by bringing up the same examples again. I can try to think of something else if you need me to? I really just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Do you often feel like your thoughts are hard to put into words?

Oh, I feel terrible... I think I've just been repeating myself this whole time, haven't I? I'm so sorry, I must be making this really tedious for you. I promise I'm trying to be clear. 

But yes, it's very hard to put into words. It's like... well, like I mentioned before, I'll try to explain something, and my mind just jumps. I'll be talking about the forklift sheets from work, and then suddenly I'm talking about the church signs down the road, and then how my husband was sounding... and I don't mean to jump around like that. It's just that it all makes sense in my head, but when it comes out, people tell me they have no idea what I'm talking about. 

I'm really trying to get better at it, though. I know it's probably annoying for people to listen to. I hope I'm answering this the way you need me to? I really want to be helpful.
Do you often find it hard to keep your thoughts in a logical order?

Oh my goodness, I am so, so sorry. You're having to ask me this again, which means I'm definitely not explaining it right. I must be the most frustrating person you've talked to all day, and I really don't want to be a bother. 

But yes, the logical order... that's exactly it. It's just like I've been saying, I try so hard to keep it straight, but when I try to explain what's going on, the order just gets all messed up. My words will just run from the forklift sheets at work, over to the church signs, and then to my husband's tone. It's not that I'm trying to be confusing, I promise! It's just... people tell me they can't follow me when I get like that. 

I feel awful that I keep giving you the exact same example. Is there a different way you need me to answer? I can try to think of something else if it helps you. I just really want to make sure I'm doing a good job for you.
Do you think the voice you hear telling you to check your pallets is coming from inside your head or from somewhere outside?

Oh, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound crazy or anything, because I'm really trying to just be honest with you. I know it probably sounds strange... but it actually sounds like it's coming from outside. Like a real person. 

Sometimes when I'm in the aisle at work, or even just at home folding clothes in my living room, I'll hear this man's voice. It's clear as day, just right there, saying, "Nicole, check it again." And... I'll look around, and there's absolutely nobody near me. 

I'm so sorry if that sounds weird or if it's not what you were expecting me to say. I know it's probably not normal... but I swear I'm not making it up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right for you.
Have your thoughts about people watching you and changing your pallet counts ever changed or wavered over time?

Oh, I really want to give you the right answer here, but... no, my thoughts on it haven't really wavered. I know I probably shouldn't say it like this, because I really don't want you to think I'm a difficult person or... or paranoid or anything. 

I actually only came in to see you because my husband and the people at the warehouse keep acting like I'm crazy. They really do, and it makes me feel awful because I try so hard to do a good job and get along with everyone. But... I just know they've been watching my moves. I know they're changing the pallet counts on me. It's just to keep me from getting that supervisor spot that I've been working so hard for. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, and I hate even saying bad things about my husband or the people I work with. I hope you don't think less of me for saying it. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to hear.
Do you often find it hard to think clearly about other things in your life, outside of work and the issues with your pallet counts?

Oh, um... I don't think so? I really hope that's an okay answer. I try so hard to keep everything else running smoothly, you know? Like, when I'm at home doing the laundry or making dinner for my husband, I can focus on that just fine. My mind doesn't really get all jumbled up with that normal everyday stuff. It's really just... well, just the work things we were talking about. 

I hope I'm not disappointing you or messing up your notes by saying no. I just haven't really noticed it being hard to think about other things outside of the warehouse. Is it bad if I say that? I can try to sit here and think really hard if maybe I'm forgetting something... I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you often find it hard to think clearly about the supervisor spot and how to get it, outside of the issues with your pallet counts?

Oh, um... I really want to give you a good answer for this, so I'll try to explain it the best I can. I guess... well, I try my hardest to focus on it, I really do. But sometimes, when I try to explain what is going on with the supervisor job and my plans, I kind of... 

I hope this doesn't make me sound silly or scatterbrained. But my words just start running all over the place. Like, I'll start out talking about the forklift sheets, and then somehow I'm talking about the church signs down the street, and then my husband's tone of voice... I don't even mean to do it, I swear. I just want to be understood, but people tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm a mess, and I hate admitting it because I really do try to be clear. I promise I'm trying. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
